channel.title: The Grant Desk - Media Arts, Film & Sound, UK, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Media Arts, Film & Sound, UK, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: BFI NETWORK England: Early Development Fund (GBP 3,000-5,000 treatment awards for debut long-form writers) (closes 11 Nov)
item.description:
BFI NETWORK (BFI, National Lottery funding)
Deadline: 11 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 3,000 to 5,000 per project to develop a treatment (stage one). Projects completed to schedule can then apply for second-stage funding to write a full first draft. National Lottery funding; no application fee stated.

BFI NETWORK's Early Development Fund supports writers at the very start of a debut long-form project: those who do not yet have a first draft of a script (or the equivalent format for immersive work).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: 2027 KCCUK Open Call for Emerging Korean Artists (Korean Cultural Centre UK) (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
Korean Cultural Centre UK (KCCUK)
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 250 participant support fee per selected artist (number of artists not stated), plus exhibition space, invigilation, opening event and KCCUK press/social promotion. Artists cover production, transport and installation costs. No application fee.

The Korean Cultural Centre UK's annual open call for emerging Korean or Korean-heritage artists, particularly UK art school graduates, leading to a group exhibition from February to April 2027 (exact dates to be confirmed).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Connected Canvas: The National Gallery Digital Commission 2027 (emerging UK creatives) (closes 17 Nov)
item.description:
National Gallery (National Gallery X), London
Deadline: 17 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 15,000 commission. Up to 10 shortlisted applicants receive GBP 500 each to develop proposals.

National Gallery X commissions a new digital, generative, screen-based or sound work for its three-screen LED canvas in the gallery. Open to UK-based emerging creatives in their first five years of practice who are not in full-time education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cryptic Nights 2027/28 Open Call (sound, performance and technology, Scotland) (closes 19 Nov)
item.description:
Cryptic, Glasgow
Deadline: 19 Nov 2026, 12:00 GMT
Award: GBP 800 fee for solo artists, up to GBP 2,000 for groups, plus residency days, mentoring, travel and access budgets.

Cryptic Nights supports emerging Scotland-based artists making work that combines original sound or music with performance, screen or technology, to develop an existing piece and present it in Cryptic's programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Radical Sabbatical 2027: six-month residencies on touch at the University of Birmingham (GBP 3,500 fee + GBP 500 production, UK-based artists) (closes 20 Nov)
item.description:
Eastside Projects with University Collections, University of Birmingham
Deadline: 20 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 3,500 artist fee plus GBP 500 production budget per artist; two artists selected.

Radical Sabbatical is a collaboration between Eastside Projects and University Collections at the University of Birmingham that gives two artists a six-month residency centred on research and development.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Youth Music: Trailblazer Fund (Round 14) (closes 20 Nov)
item.description:
Youth Music
Deadline: 20 Nov 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: GBP 2,000 to GBP 30,000 for organisations in England. No application fee.

Youth Music's Trailblazer Fund gives GBP 2,000 to GBP 30,000 to organisations in England running projects that let children and young people aged 25 or under make, learn and earn in music.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Futures of Listening x Immersive Audio Network: Residency Open Call (Bristol, IAN Festival 2027) (closes 21 Nov)
item.description:
Futures of Listening (FIBER, 4DSOUND, Robin Koek, Art of Sound) and the Immersive Audio Network (IAN)
Deadline: 21 Nov 2026, 23:59 CET
Award: EUR 1,750 residency fee (excl. VAT, paid on invoice), plus return travel from the Netherlands to Bristol and private accommodation for 22 to 30 January 2027. No application fee.

One residency for a freelance audio practitioner (composer, sound designer, audio maker, artist or researcher) registered in the Netherlands, to develop an existing project into a spatial, story-led sound work.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Refugee Festival Scotland 2027 x Opening Shot: Open Call for First-Time Filmmakers (GBP 1,500 fee plus GBP 3,000 production budget) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Refugee Festival Scotland (Scottish Refugee Council) with Opening Shot
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026
Award: GBP 1,500 participation fee plus a GBP 3,000 production budget per filmmaker, with mentoring and a premiere screening at Refugee Festival Scotland in June 2027. Four filmmakers selected. No application fee stated.

Refugee Festival Scotland (run by the Scottish Refugee Council, festival 11 to 20 June 2027) and Opening Shot invite four first-time filmmakers with lived experience of seeking safety to make a short film of about five minutes.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Hidden Door 2027: Visual Art Open Call (Edinburgh, up to GBP 1,500 per artwork, Scotland-based artists) (closes 3 Dec)
item.description:
Hidden Door Festival
Deadline: 3 Dec 2026
Award: Up to GBP 1,500 per artwork/application, covering all artist fees and expenses, budgeted against Scottish Artists' Union rates (most awards will be lower). No application fee.

Hidden Door is a volunteer-run, multi-arts festival that reopens disused and overlooked buildings in Edinburgh.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Youth Music: Recharge Fund, Racial Equity (up to GBP 120,000 core funding over four years) (closes 4 Dec)
item.description:
Youth Music
Deadline: 4 Dec 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: Core funding of up to GBP 120,000 over four years per organisation, from a total pot of GBP 2,400,000. No application fee.

Youth Music's Recharge Fund: Racial Equity gives multi-year core funding to creative organisations across England that are led by communities who experience racial injustice and that work with children and/or young people of different ages and backgrounds.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cove Park Awarded Residencies 2027-2028 (Scotland, UK, Central and South America and diasporas) (closes 11 Dec)
item.description:
Cove Park
Deadline: 11 Dec 2026, 17:00 GMT
Award: Fully funded: GBP 775 per week fee (VAT inclusive, freelance), travel allowance (Scotland GBP 65 to 200, rest of UK up to GBP 250, Europe up to GBP 400, other international up to GBP 1,250), materials up to GBP 150 for studio-based practitioners, private accommodation and studio, visa and access support. Application Access Bursary available (request by 30 November 2026). No application fee.

Cove Park's biennial call for fully funded Awarded Residencies at its 50-acre rural residency site in Argyll, on the west coast of Scotland, programmed between May 2027 and December 2028.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: EVA London 2027: Call for Proposals (Electronic Visualisation and the Arts, 12-16 July 2027) (closes 11 Jan 2027)
item.description:
EVA London (BCS Computer Arts Society)
Deadline: 11 Jan 2027
Award: NO CASH, listed as an exception at the editor's request (conference presentation slot and publication in the proceedings). Free to submit, but at least one author of each paper and all panel and workshop presenters must pay conference registration (rates not yet published; to be set in spring 2027, with a special rate for Research Workshop presenters).

EVA London is a long-running hybrid conference on electronic visualisation and the arts, covering digital art, creative technology, computing and visual culture, held at BCS in Moorgate, London, and online.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Sheffield DocFest 2027: Film Programme Entries (34th edition, 9-14 June 2027) (closes 19 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Sheffield DocFest
Deadline: 19 Feb 2027
Award: NO PUBLISHED CASH, listed under the desk's festival exception (selection for the festival programme; award amounts not stated on the entry page). Entry fees: features and mid-length films over 40 minutes GBP 40 early (to 20 November 2026), GBP 48 standard (to 29 January 2027), GBP 58 late (to 19 February 2027); shorts under 40 minutes GBP 30 / GBP 38 / GBP 48 on the same dates (plus VAT as listed). Student and film-school discounts on request.

Sheffield DocFest, the UK's leading documentary festival, is open for film entries to its June 2027 edition, for feature, mid-length and short documentaries and non-fiction series.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Creative Debuts: Black Artists Grant (BAG), GBP 500 monthly no-strings grant for UK-based Black artists (rolling)
item.description:
Creative Debuts
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: GBP 500 per recipient, one recipient per month. Unrestricted, no outcomes or reporting required. No application fee.

The Black Artists Grant (BAG) is a no-strings-attached monthly grant run and sponsored by Creative Debuts, the London-based platform for emerging artists.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Alpaca Festival 2027: Open Call for Pattern-Based Performances, Workshops and Talks (Sheffield, UK)
item.description: Pattern Club (Alpaca Festival) · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · Performances: artist fee plus national travel expenses. Workshops: artist fee, materials expenses and national travel expenses. Fee amounts are not yet confirmed (tight budget); additional costs may be covered on request. International travel is not covered beyond a small European train budget. Conference talks: no fee or expenses, in-person speakers get a free festival weekend pass and lunch on 6 and 7 May. No application fee.

item.title: BRAID Creative Commissions 2027: A Promise in Return (Responsible AI, GBP 8,000-12,000, Edinburgh Art Festival)
item.description: BRAID (Bridging Responsible AI Divides), University of Edinburgh, with Inspace, the Institute for Design Informatics and the Edinburgh Futures Institute · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · Around seven commissions with budgets of GBP 8,000 to 12,000 each, inclusive of VAT and all costs. No application fee.

item.title: Creative Scotland: Open Fund for Individuals (rolling)
item.description: Creative Scotland · deadline Rolling / undated · GBP 500 to GBP 50,000 (two levels: up to GBP 20,000 with decisions in 10 weeks, GBP 20,001 to 50,000 in 14 weeks). National Lottery funded. No application fee.

item.title: The Photographers' Gallery: Future of Archives, Whose Archive is it Anyway? (Call for Speakers)
item.description: The Photographers' Gallery · deadline 01 Nov 2026 · GBP 200 speaker fee for each selected speaker. No application fee.
